clue.text: Foreign student among one thousand, perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters given are only one possible arrangement, so they may be rearranged

parts.note: L for learner, the usual crossword student

explanation.surface: A foreign student is one among a thousand others at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish describes something strange or alien, the older sense being from abroad, so it matches foreign.

clue.text: Chances old theologian will be seen on Sunday?

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Is it likely an elderly theologian will turn up at church on Sunday?
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the probabilities of something happening, as quoted by bookmakers, so they are chances.

clue.text: Present, child's plaything broken by American lawyer

indicators.note: a thing broken by something has that thing in its middle

explanation.surface: A child's gift is broken by an American lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Today as a noun means the present time, as opposed to the past or future.

clue.text: Way of selling uranium featured in court case

indicators.note: featured in means placed within another word

parts.note: a legal action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A method of selling uranium becomes the subject of a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction goods go to the highest bidder, a public method of sale.

clue.text: Daughter's given greasy napkin

explanation.surface: A daughter is handed a grease-stained serviette.
explanation.definitionFit: A doily is a small ornamental mat of lace or paper, historically also a small table napkin.

clue.text: Feeling engendered by last pair of woollen mittens

indicators.note: something engendered is freshly produced, so new letters are formed from old
'last pair of' keeps only the final two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A pair of woolly mittens stirs warm emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an emotion or attitude, so it is a synonym of a feeling.

clue.text: Grease needed in camera?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Grease is a musical movie of 1978
second meaning: the light-sensitive strip loaded into a traditional camera

explanation.walkthrough: Grease looks like lubricant for the camera's works, but it is the title of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is one example of a movie, and a traditional camera cannot take pictures without the photographic strip loaded.

clue.text: Mix with other pupils to do some calculus?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring into a school community
second meaning: to find the area under a curve

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to join a group as an equal member and to perform the calculus operation inverse to differentiation.

clue.text: Ethical systems one's encountered in some trial, perhaps

indicators.note: encountered in means met inside, placing one piece within the other
'perhaps' says the letters given are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone meets various moral codes during a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Moralities are particular codes of right and wrong conduct, so they are sets of ethics.

clue.text: Quantity of wine oriental students loaded into vehicle

indicators.note: loaded into means packed inside, so these pieces sit within another

explanation.surface: Students from the East pack a stock of wine into a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar can mean a stock of wine kept by a person, not only the underground room.

clue.text: Cut in payment from Sherlock Holmes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an amount taken off wages or a bill
second meaning: the detective's famous reasoning from clues

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a subtraction from a sum owed and the logical inference the fictional detective was famous for making.

clue.text: Some recent errors appearing in register

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the following words, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A clerk notices a few recent mistakes in the official register.
explanation.definitionFit: To register an item is to record it formally in a list or book, just as to enter it.

clue.text: Reveal characteristics of young folk, primarily — pity to make changes

indicators.note: making changes to a word means its letters are reordered
'primarily' means in the first place, so only the opening letter of each of the two words is used

parts.note: the initials of the two words

explanation.surface: It is a pity young people must keep changing in order to show who they are.
explanation.definitionFit: To typify something is to be a representative example of it, showing its essential qualities.

clue.text: Unwell having knocked back most of drink that's illicit

indicators.note: knocking back a drink turns it up, so the shortened word is read backwards
'most of' means the word is used minus its final letter

parts.note: lager is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone feels sick after downing most of a drink that was smuggled or otherwise unlawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illicit is forbidden by law, which is exactly what unlawful conduct is.

clue.text: Confection evokes inordinate cackles among squiffy EEC representatives

indicators.note: inordinate means out of order, so letters are rearranged
squiffy is British slang for tipsy, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the representatives are the letters of the abbreviation itself

explanation.surface: A sweet treat makes tipsy European officials laugh raucously.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eccles cake is a small round flaky pastry filled with currants, from Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry with sugared currant filling counts as a sweet confection.

clue.text: Very bad French article, a matter of record?

parts.note: informal British sense of chronic: dreadful

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dreadful French newspaper piece is now on the record.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang chronic means terrible, not just long-lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written historical account of events in order, so it is something kept on record.

clue.text: Plan which resolves anxieties?

parts.note: surface reading: a scheme that eases worries
setter's reading: a chart that renders hills and valleys in raised form

explanation.walkthrough: Relief means both easing of stress and raised land shown on a chart; plan means a drawn chart, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a chart showing landscape height, and the first word also means release from worry.

clue.text: Craft exemplified in a cart a man repaired

indicators.note: repaired things are put back together, here in a different order

explanation.surface: A craftsman fixes a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, and craft is a general word for a vessel.

clue.text: Criticise cook

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to attack or mock harshly
second meaning: to cook meat in an oven

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like complaining about a chef; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to bake meat in an oven and, informally, to deride someone severely in public.

clue.text: Plant Cilla's cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated ground is turned over, so the name is worked into another order

explanation.surface: A gardener called Cilla has grown a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering shrub with scented purple or white blossom, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Finance required for operation, removing front tooth

indicators.note: an operation works on something, here reworking letters
removing the front means dropping the first letter

explanation.surface: Funding is needed for surgery to extract a front tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is the pointed tooth between the incisors and the premolars.

clue.text: French conversation

parts.note: surface reading: a chat conducted in the French language
setter's reading: a private talk between two people, named by a phrase borrowed from French

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally means head to head in French and is used in English for an intimate chat.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed phrase describes a private discussion between two people, so it is a conversation of French origin.

clue.text: Not in favour of getting kitchen range this month

parts.note: Aga is a British brand of heavy cast-iron range cooker
inst., short for instant, is old business shorthand for this month

explanation.surface: Someone objects to buying a new cooker this month.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is the preposition for opposing something, the opposite of being for it.

clue.text: Bone set in plaster, numbed

indicators.note: 'set in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A broken bone has been put in a cast, and the patient is numb.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat breastbone in the centre of the chest, so it is a bone.

clue.text: Study about a small business, produced by Brodie?

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a study about a small firm was written by a man called Brodie.
explanation.walkthrough: Deacon Brodie was an 18th-century Edinburgh cabinet-maker and town councillor who led a double life as a burglar.
explanation.definitionFit: Brodie's title came from his office as head of a trades guild, so the question mark points to his famous nickname.

clue.text: Noble Conservative basking in reflected praise

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word reads backwards
basking in something means being surrounded by it

explanation.surface: A Tory aristocrat enjoys reflected glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means relating to a duke, the highest rank of the British nobility.

clue.text: Willow, very big, that is found beside river

explanation.surface: A huge willow tree grows on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a species of willow whose pliant shoots are used in basketwork.

clue.text: Wild duck leaves loch

parts.note: standard abbreviation for lake or loch

explanation.surface: A wild duck flies away from a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departure but is the noun, as in dried leaves for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling bird, a species of wild duck.

clue.text: Amend material provided by publicists

indicators.note: material is raw stuff to be fashioned, so the word before it is reshaped

explanation.surface: Copy written by the advertising team needs correcting.
explanation.definitionFit: Admen work in advertising, and publicists are people whose job is promoting products or clients.

clue.text: Square coin, unusually, found in broken creel

indicators.note: 'found in' places one group of letters inside another
done unusually means not in the normal order

parts.note: taken as written; a creel is a fishing basket

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces to be put back together differently

explanation.surface: An oddly square coin turns up in a broken fishing basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To square accounts or differing views is to make them agree, which is to reconcile them.

clue.text: Catch sight of a group of snakes — pythons, typically

indicators.note: a group of letters is a small cluster taken from within the words

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone spots a nest of snakes, which are most likely pythons.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is a literary verb for noticing or glimpsing something at a distance.

clue.text: One-sided article contributes to abnormal ill-nature

indicators.note: abnormal means out of the regular order, so letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An essay contributes to an unusual ill temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A unilateral action is taken by one party alone, without agreement from the other side.
